issues.legal_issue: An allottee of acquired evacuee property retains sufficient interest to seek judicial review of action affecting the allotted land.
material_facts: The respondents had received an allotment of land and remained in possession under a quasi-permanent tenure.
The Central Government acquired the evacuee property before the respondents filed their writ petition, but the respondents continued in possession on the conditions governing their allotment.
The respondents filed their petition before receiving a sanad, which conferred proprietary rights before the High Court finally disposed of the petition.
issues.conclusion: The respondents had sufficient interest to maintain their petition under Article 226, notwithstanding the acquisition notification issued before they filed it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 10 and 12 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, read with rule 14(6) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Rules, 1950, preserved an allottee’s valuable quasi-permanent interest while the property remained vested in the Central Government. The Court relied on Amar Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Punjab, which recognized that such rights were entitled to protection by the courts; the subsequent sanad conferred full proprietary rights.

rule.if: displaced_person_allotment and acquired_allotted_property and continued_possession and writ_petition

predicates.displaced_person_allotment: A displaced person received an allotment of property under an evacuee-property arrangement.
predicates.acquired_allotted_property: The government acquired the property that had been allotted to the displaced person.
predicates.continued_possession: The allottee remained in possession under the conditions of the allotment after the acquisition.
predicates.writ_petition: The allottee brought a petition seeking judicial review of action affecting the allotted property.
predicates.writ_petition_maintainable: The allottee may maintain the petition seeking judicial review.

issues.definition: When a displaced person’s allotted property is acquired but the person remains in possession under the allotment conditions, the person may maintain a petition seeking judicial review of action affecting that property.

issues.legal_issue: A consolidation scheme cannot replace an allottee’s holding with land of lesser value without providing equal-value land or compensation, and administrative directions cannot authorize that result.
material_facts: In a consolidation proceeding, the respondents’ originally allotted holding was replaced with land of admittedly lesser value.
No compensation was paid for the difference in value.
The Consolidation Officer formulated the scheme pursuant to administrative directions from the State Government, and the scheme was confirmed on that basis.
No statutory authority empowering the State Government to issue those directions was shown.
issues.conclusion: The confirmation of the scheme was illegal, and the High Court rightly set it aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, 1948, requires a consolidation scheme to provide compensation when an owner receives a holding of lesser market value and to recover compensation when an owner receives a holding of greater market value. The Act does not empower the Consolidation Officer to deprive an owner of value without equal-value land or compensation, nor does it empower the State Government to issue directions controlling the exercise of the officer’s statutory powers; directions repugnant to the Act cannot validate such a scheme.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and lower_value_replacement and no_compensation and scheme_based_on_administrative_directions and no_statutory_authority_shown

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: Officials prepared and confirmed a scheme to consolidate agricultural holdings.
predicates.lower_value_replacement: The scheme gave an owner replacement land of lesser value than the owner’s original holding.
predicates.no_compensation: The owner received no compensation for the difference in value.
predicates.scheme_based_on_administrative_direction: The consolidation official formulated the scheme in reliance on directions issued by the government.
predicates.no_statutory_authority_shown: The government did not identify statutory authority for issuing directions controlling the consolidation official’s exercise of statutory powers.
predicates.scheme_confirmation_invalid: The confirmation of the scheme is invalid.

issues.definition: When a consolidation scheme replaces an owner’s holding with lower-value land without compensation, relies on government administrative directions, and no statutory authority for those directions is shown, the scheme’s confirmation is invalid.
